title: Ampule-sealed Acidolysis for Monosaccharide Composition Analysis of Serum or Plasma Samples
protocol: Collect leftover serum samples after their clinical tests at the hospital.
Divide each serum sample into three aliquots in 1.5 mL EP tubes and store at -80°C.
Thaw serum samples on ice.
Transfer 10 μL of serum sample into a 2 mL ampoule.
Add 10 μL Rha (1 mg/mL) to the ampoule.
Add 1 mL TFA (2M) to each ampoule.
Conduct acidolysis in an oil bath for 6 hours.
Transfer the samples to 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes and dry them in a centrifugal concentrator.
Add 200 μL of chromatographic methanol to the samples, vortex thoroughly, and concentrate and dry the mixture three times to obtain cleaner hydrolyzed samples.
Add 40 μL NaOH (0.3M) and 60 μL PMP (0.5M) into each sample.
Vortex for 5 seconds and centrifuge for another 10 seconds.
Conduct PMP derivatization reaction at 70°C in a water bath for 90 minutes.
Neutralize the reaction mixture with hydrochloric acid.
Add 500 μL CHCl3 into each sample tube.
Vortex each sample tube for 5 s.
Centrifuge samples for 10 min at 13,000 g/min.
Transfer the supernatant to HPLC vials.
Dilute stock solutions of Man, GlcN, GalN, GlcUA, Glc, Gal, Xyl, Fuc, Rha to 1.0 mg/mL.
Mix diluted monosaccharide standards and dilute further by a factor of two.
Add 40 μL 0.3 M NaOH into each standard mixture to adjust pH to 12-13.
Tune the LC system according to manufacturers’ recommendations or laboratory SOP.
Set up the HPLC system to separate PMP-labeled monosaccharides as described under EQUIPMENT SETUP.
Follow extraction conditions in Steps 9-10 to avoid high background caused by leftover PMP.
Ensure the LC-MS system is functioning properly and DAD wavelength is set at 254 nm.
Check pH value of Step 7; ensure it is between 11 and 13 for efficient PMP-derivatization.
Calculate monosaccharide contents based on the regression equation of the monosaccharide standards.
